The claim states that $Sigma$ is a $3 x 3$ symmetric positive-definite matrix. The evidence describes $Sigma$ as a geometric parameter of an ellipsoidal primitive, appearing in the quadratic form $d^T Sigma^{-1} d$. In the context of 3D geometry and ellipsoids, the matrix defining the shape (covariance-like matrix) must be symmetric and positive-definite to represent a valid ellipsoid. Furthermore, since the displacement vector $d$ is defined in 3D space ($x - mu$ where $x$ and $mu$ are 3D coordinates), the matrix $Sigma$ must be $3 x 3$ to allow the matrix multiplication. Therefore, all facts in the claim are supported by the mathematical context provided in the evidence.
